question.problem: Find the shortest distance between the point $P(3,5,-2)$ and the plane $Π$ with equation $(r-[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 9 \\ 0\end{aligned}])\cdot [\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 2 \\ -4\end{aligned}]=0.$
question.worked_solution:
Let's pick a point on the plane, for instance, $Q(5,9,0).$ Then 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 9 \\ 0\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 5 \\ -2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4 \\ 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Also, from the equation of the plane, we get a normal vector $n=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 2 \\ -4\end{aligned}].$

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|2\cdot (-2)+4\cdot 2+2\cdot (-4)|}{\sqrt{(-2)^{2}+{2}^{2}+(-4)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|-4+8-8|}{\sqrt{4+4+16}} \\  & =\frac{|-4|}{\sqrt{24}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{6}}{3}\end{aligned}
$$
